abstract.p: Walking is widely recommended. HbA1c fell by 0.6 percentage points.

sec.title: Methods
sec.p: We enrolled 412 adults aged 40–75 years at four community clinics1.

sec.title: Outcomes
sec.p: The primary outcome was the change in HbA1c at 12 weeks.

sec.title: Results
sec.p: Of the 412 participants, 389 completed follow-up. HbA1c fell by 0.6 percentage points in the walking group compared with 0.1 in usual care (difference 0.5; 95% CI 0.3 to 0.7; p<0.001).

sec.title: Limitations
sec.p: Follow-up lasted only 12 weeks, so we cannot say whether the benefit persists.
